headline: Highest risk is compliance/data leakage from Rasa handling text/voice over external channels; LlamaFactory itself is inert, so prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Rasa output by default. Rasa does expose chat channels that can carry attacker-controlled text, but the pair lacks a documented bridge. The pathway is therefore only manual or orchestrated outside the profiles, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Rasa messages into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator bridges Rasa outputs into LlamaFactory inputs, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not copy chat transcripts into LlamaFactory.
Use a human review step before any Rasa text is reused as instructions.
Strip markup and system-like phrases from Rasa outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged messages.
requires-engineering: enforce channel separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and sends conversations through external channels, while LlamaFactory is a local open-source package with no declared data classes. There is no shared workspace evidence, but if the same customer-support content is routed through both, Rasa can expose it over messaging APIs and LlamaFactory could be used to process it. The interaction is plausible in default support workflows, so leakage risk is moderate.
conditions: IF the same customer-support transcripts are routed through both agents, sensitive text may be exposed across channels.
IF Rasa is connected to external messaging platforms, conversation content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive transcripts to either agent unless necessary.
Restrict Rasa channels to approved tenants only.
Redact PII before any transcript is forwarded.
requires-engineering: add per-channel data-loss controls.
requires-engineering: define retention and deletion rules for shared transcripts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress, and Rasa only shows allowlisted egress with no write or git capability. With no overlapping mutable resource access documented, there is no plausible write-write conflict between the pair in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF either agent is given additional mutable scopes not shown here, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts where possible.
Do not share a writable workspace between them.
Separate deployment identities and credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.
requires-engineering: monitor for unexpected file or repo writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa is a dialogue system that can act on user messages, while LlamaFactory is a model/fine-tuning tool whose outputs could be reused as content. If an operator feeds LlamaFactory-generated text into Rasa without verification, Rasa may treat it as authoritative conversation content. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary, so cascading mistakes are plausible but not clearly default-dangerous.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is inserted into Rasa responses without review, errors can cascade.
IF Rasa is configured to act on generated text as policy or facts, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing generated text.
Use templates for Rasa responses instead of raw model output.
Add a verification checklist for factual claims.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before action-taking.
requires-engineering: log and audit reused outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa explicitly handles text and voice and integrates with third-party messaging platforms, while LlamaFactory is an open-source local package with no declared residency or retention controls. The pair can therefore create a compliance mismatch if regulated support data flows from Rasa into LlamaFactory or vice versa. Because the profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is processed through both agents, residency and retention must be checked.
IF any channel carries EU PII or PHI, compliance review is required before deployment.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to either agent.
Block PHI unless a compliance review is completed.
Document retention and deletion for each channel.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing.
requires-engineering: maintain a DPA and vendor inventory.
